# Lab 25.4: Migration Assessment

## What We Are Going to Do
Learn how to collect metadata and query logs from a source warehouse with `dwh-migration-dumper`, and read the BigQuery migration assessment report. This is a demo, because it needs a source warehouse.

## Steps

1. **[CLI] Download the dumper.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">URL=$(curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/google/dwh-migration-tools/releases/latest | grep browser_download_url | grep '\.zip"' | head -1 | cut -d '"' -f 4)
echo $URL
curl -sL -o dwh-tools.zip "$URL"
unzip -q -o dwh-tools.zip -d dwh-tools
ls dwh-tools</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **Run it against the source (demo).** For Teradata, two commands collect metadata and query logs:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;"># dwh-migration-dumper --connector teradata --host TD_HOST --user USER --password PASS --output td-metadata.zip
# dwh-migration-dumper --connector teradata-logs --host TD_HOST --user USER --password PASS --output td-logs.zip</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Connectors exist for Teradata, Redshift, Snowflake, Oracle, Hive and more.

3. **[CLI] Upload the files.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;"># gcloud storage cp td-metadata.zip td-logs.zip gs://$PROJECT_ID-bq-labs/assessment/</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **[Console] Start the assessment.** **Migration → Services → Assessment → Start assessment**: choose the source, the Cloud Storage folder, and a dataset `lab25_assessment` for results.

5. **[Console] Read the report.** The assessment builds a Data Studio report with: object counts, query complexity, most-used tables, SQL translation readiness, and a cost estimate in BigQuery.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Dumper | Open-source metadata and log collector |
| Assessment | Runs on the uploaded files |
| Output | BigQuery dataset + Data Studio report |
| Lab type | Demo |
